answers: Test round 18's one failure: CI run 41393622961 at b59a0203, job 125113156314, failed TestPodUpdateTellsItsWorkerNothingHoweverTheRoundEnds/the_pod_went_without_its_round at podupdate_test.go:1188 with `timed out waiting for implementer: its round to end`, which the tester reproduced at about 3 in 60 subtest runs. One test file changed; no production code.

proof.criterion: A wait whose condition only a sweep can bring about sweeps under its bound, as awaitReplacement already did. rig.tick() is one sweep and in this rig no sweep happens unless a test calls for one, so polling can never satisfy such a condition when the single tick decides nothing — the sweep reads the claims through the deciding mask and leaves the decision to the next sweep.
proof.surface: The daemon's orphan sweep over a real PostgreSQL with real claim machines, run at the repetition the flake was measured at. The server is this role's own at 127.0.0.1:5455, so no sibling of the pod shares it.
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/daemon 179.265s — 100 runs of all three subtests, 0 failures. Run by the implementer, not quoted from a subagent.
proof.negativeControl: The defect was reproduced on the unchanged file at 2 in 40 runs of the same command, both times `podupdate_test.go:1188: timed out waiting for implementer: its round to end` in the subtest `the_pod_went_without_its_round`; CI's own run 41393622961 is the third reproduction, and the tester's own PostgreSQL gave 3 in 60 and then 4 more.

proof.criterion: The change weakens no assertion and touches nothing but the one test file.
proof.surface: The repository's own checks and the whole pod-update family at the head.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && gofmt -l ./internal/ && go vet ./internal/... && LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5455/postgres?sslmode=disable go test -count=1 -timeout 25m ./internal/daemon/ -run 'PodUpdate|StalePlugin|PodRound|Update|Displaced|Drift'; and jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" diff --name-only
proof.observed: gofmt prints nothing, vet clean, ok internal/daemon 31.3s with 43 PASS. `jj diff --name-only` lists exactly one path, packages/daemon/internal/daemon/podupdate_test.go. The failing subtest's body now waits for every seeded role's round before the end under test, which adds a requirement rather than removing one.
proof.negativeControl: Each of the three subtests still asserts exactly what it asserted before — that the worker is told nothing however the round ends — and the one that caught the real cause fails if the extra wait is removed, because the sweep then opens a round over the replacement pod and sends the worker an ask.

proof.criterion: The rest of the daemon module is unaffected.
proof.surface: The whole Go suite of the packages this branch touches.
proof.observed: internal/supervise ok (113.0s), internal/runtime ok, runtime/fake ok, runtime/sandbox ok (269.9s), runtime/shellprefix ok, runtime/workerbin ok, internal/api ok (157.8s), internal/store ok (57.2s), store/migrations ok, internal/prompts ok. The one failure anywhere is internal/runtime/tmux's TestNewRefusesLaunchersItCannotRun, which needs tmux on PATH and this pod has none.
proof.negativeControl: The same tmux failure, and no other, is present at every earlier head of this branch and on a fresh clone of main; it is the environment, not the change.

movedToTheSweepingWait: the worker to be asked again, past the re-task bound — the re-ask is the sweep's own post, and the rig's clock is held so no second ask can follow an extra sweep
its round to end — the defect's own site, where tickBackIn's single sweep may decide nothing
its plugin round to end — reconcilePluginUpdate is the sweep's, and an extra end-post relaunches nothing on a suspended claim
the suspended claim to be revived for the round — the revive is the sweep's openPodUpdate, and a second post finds the claim launching and resumes nothing
leftPollingAndWhy: Every awaitRound: the sweep has already posted the round and the machine merely records it, so polling is what that wait is for.

Every wait for a round's end that follows a proved decision — an awaitReplacement, a messages() count, or the endRoundOverAGonePod log line just above it. Sweeping there is not free: openPodUpdate re-asks every blocking claim of a round whose end has landed on one claim and not its neighbour, so an extra sweep could reopen the round it is waiting to see end. The file already shows that hazard at the end of the gone-pod test, where a deliberate extra tick opens a fresh round over the still-drifted pod.
Waits on a direct call handled asynchronously: an ask retiring with its turn, an operator's or the daemon's suspension letting its process go, and an end the test itself posts.
The wait for a round to stay open, which a negative assertion needs to hold rather than change.
The stale-plugin relaunch wait, which the test's own refreshStalePlugins decides; rig.tick() runs only reconcilePodUpdates, so sweeping could not drive it at all.

filesChanged: packages/daemon/internal/daemon/podupdate_test.go: the awaitSwept helper, four waits moved onto it, and the failing subtest's body waiting for every seeded role's round before the end under test.
trickyParts: awaitSwept's first poll deliberately sweeps nothing. An extra sweep is harmless only where no decision is in flight: completePodUpdate would replace the pod a second time, and openPodUpdate posts to every blocking claim, so a sweep that reads an end landed on one claim and not another re-asks the whole round it just ended. One poll interval lets a posted end land first, and a condition no sweep has decided still gets one sweep per poll.

Sweeping alone did not make the subtest pass, and the real cause is worth the tester's attention. The test drove tickBackIn while the tester's ask was still being written, so that claim was not yet a member of the round in the store's snapshot, lostClaims was empty, the pod-went-without-its-round branch was skipped, and the sweep opened a new round over the pod that replaced the round's own. The sweeping wait then ends that new round, which is why the timeout went away, but the stray ask it sent still failed the assertion — correctly. Waiting for every seeded role's round before the end under test closes it.
openQuestions: The production window behind that cause is the trade-off review round 8 named and accepted when the report moved to the round's own record: a claim the round has posted to, whose machine has not yet recorded the ask, is not a member, so a pod that dies inside that window has its lost work unreported and a fresh round opens over the replacement. The round re-posts every tick, so the window is one tick. It is recorded here because this round's investigation sharpened it from 'a role that registered late' to 'any claim whose machine has not yet recorded the ask', and the reviewer may want that stated in the guide rather than only in the thread.
